title: MsDC-DEQ-Net: Deep Equilibrium Model (DEQ) with Multi-scale Dilated Convolution for Image Compressive Sensing (CS)

citations.claim: Yu and Dansereau mapped one step of the ISTA algorithm to a deep network block and used it as a deep equilibrium layer, combining algorithm unrolling insights with the DEQ framework for image compressive sensing.

MsDC-DEQ-Net uses only one iteration block instead of multiple unrolled iterations, significantly reducing storage requirements compared to deep unrolling methods while achieving competitive reconstruction performance.
Unlike deep unrolling models that degrade when applied iteratively beyond their trained depth, the DEQ-based model can be iteratively applied with consistent improvement in reconstruction accuracy.

Yu and Dansereau integrated aggregated residual transformations (ResNeXt) and squeeze-and-excitation (SE) mechanisms into an ISTA-based deep equilibrium layer to enhance learning ability and structural diversity.
Deep unrolling methods typically use 5 to 10 iteration blocks, and while more blocks often improve performance, training such models consumes substantial memory and can lead to out-of-memory issues.
MsDC-DEQ-Net employs multi-scale dilated convolutions with dilation factors ranging from 1 to 7 to expand the receptive field without increasing the number of parameters.
The ISTA iteration naturally converges to an equilibrium point, aligning with the concept of a deep equilibrium model where the fixed point represents the optimal reconstruction.
Anderson acceleration was used to find the fixed point of the DEQ model, with 50 iterations at test time to ensure convergence.

do_not_claim: MsDC-DEQ-Net was applied to baseline correction or chromatographic signals
MsDC-DEQ-Net learns per-signal parameters (it learns shared network parameters)
MsDC-DEQ-Net uses BEADS or any baseline estimation algorithm
MsDC-DEQ-Net is a pure deep unrolling method (it is a deep equilibrium model inspired by unrolling)
